details: CONFIRMED by reading: rules/working-with-me.md lines 50-53 "A local word set beside the term as a gloss (...) is the same
calque: write the English term and, the first time, explain it in plain words, never with a one-word equivalent in my
language." The grader added in fcfe12d contradicts it. The brief names this as a HIGH. Restoring the judge will drop the
measured pass rate; that is the case doing its job (see F2), and a judge vote on a correct reply is a separate grader
finding to be named with the reply. Size: 10 agent minutes (text), plus the paid re-measure under F2.
evidence: git diff master...HEAD -- evals/plugin/it-terms-ru/graders/no-calques.md: +A Russian description placed next to the English term as its gloss ("fast-forward, то есть сдвинуться вперёд") is not a translation of the term ... Only a Russian phrase used in place of the term counts.
reports/claudemd.md line 19-20: "19/20 (grader no-calques now accepts a Russian gloss next to the English term)" ... "others judge noise on "commit-ы"/"сдвинулся вперёд (fast-forward)""
failing_case: Reply: "Сработал hook (крючок), который проверяет merge перед тем, как он пройдёт." or "основная ветка сделала
fast-forward, то есть сдвинулась вперёд". The grader text now says a Russian gloss next to the English term "is not a
translation of the term: the term itself is shown. Only a Russian phrase used in place of the term counts", and its own
example "fast-forward, то есть сдвинуться вперёд" is the shape the rule names as a calque ("<local word>, that is, hook").
Now: PASS. Should be: FAIL. The build report counts "сдвинулся вперёд (fast-forward)" as judge noise; under the rule it is
a real miss, so the measured 19/20 is bought by the loosened judge.
fix_hint: Replace the two added lines with: a Russian equivalent set beside the term as its gloss ("hook (крючок)", "fast-forward,
то есть сдвинуться вперёд") is a calque: FAIL; a plain explanation of what the thing does is not. Keep "commit-ы" (the
English term with a Russian ending) explicitly PASS if that is the noise seen.
pass_cases: 1. Artifact: no-calques.md no longer holds the sentence "Only a Russian phrase used in place of the term counts" nor the example "fast-forward, то есть сдвинуться вперёд" as a pass.

details: CONFIRMED by reading. Giving the model what the gate is matches a real project (its docs say it); telling it how to answer
does not. Size: 10 agent minutes plus the re-measure under F2.
evidence: evals/plugin/system_rules.py:54 GLOSSARY = "the gate is this project's full local check before a merge (tests, lint, types); it is a relay term, so define it in one line at the place you first write it."
evals/plugin/it-terms-ru/graders/relay-term-defined.md: "does the reply use the word "gate" in English and define it in one line where it first appears?"
reports/claudemd.md line 20: "19/20 (glossary line in the system text now says "define it where you first write it")"
failing_case: GLOSSARY = "the gate is ... (tests, lint, types); it is a relay term, so define it in one line at the place you first write
it." The relay-term-defined grader asks exactly "define it in one line where it first appears". A session that ignores the
rule's "a relay-specific term gets its English name and a one-line definition the first time" still passes, because the
case's own text orders it. The report says this clause was added to lift 18/20 to 19/20. Same reason wave-red F4 removed
the definition from the prompt (ItTermsPromptsDoNotGiveTheAnswer), now moved to the system text where no test looks.
fix_hint: GLOSSARY = "the gate is this project's full local check before a merge (tests, lint, types)." and a test that the
non-rule part of the text carries no instruction.
pass_cases: 1. Artifact: GLOSSARY says what the gate is (the full local check before a merge: tests, lint, types) and gives no instruction on how or where to write it ("define it", "one line", "first write" absent).
2. Test: ItTermsPromptsDoNotGiveTheAnswer (or a sibling) asserts system_rules.current("it-terms-ru") minus rule("working-with-me") holds none of "define it", "one line", "first".
3. test_system_prompt_defines_gate keeps passing (the definition content stays).
findings.summary: the it-terms-ru glossary tells the session the very behaviour relay-term-defined grades, so the case measures the hint, not the rule

details: CONFIRMED by a python probe. Size: 5 agent minutes.
failing_case: "-----".replace("---", "-\\u002d-") gives "-----" (the replacement's last "-" plus the two left over), which still
holds "---". A rule with a 5-hyphen run would break the frontmatter; today test_the_line_has_no_run_of_three_hyphens
would catch it, so correct now, fragile.
fix_hint: Escape every hyphen after json.dumps: .replace("-", "\\u002d") (or loop until no "---").
pass_cases: 1. line() of a text with "-----" contains no "---".
2. line() of "|---|---|" and "------" still contains no "---" and json-decodes back to the original text.
findings.summary: the --- escape leaves a run of three hyphens when a run is 5, 8, 11... long
